# postgres

```go
import "github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/stores/postgres"
```

Package postgres is the PostgreSQL state\-store backend for blkit: a durable, strongly consistent, shareable store keeping each run's ProcessState in PostgreSQL, built on pgx/v5 with pgx.Batch pipelining. See specs/stores/postgres\-state\-store.spec.md.

<a name="New"></a>
### func [New](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/postgres/store.go#L45>)

```go
func New(cfg Config) *Store
```

New parses the config and creates the connection pool (connections are established lazily; the schema is created on first use). Following the blkit constructor convention it panics on an invalid config.

<a name="Store.CurrentVersion"></a>
### func (\*Store) [CurrentVersion](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/postgres/store.go#L247>)

```go
func (s *Store) CurrentVersion(runID string) (*bl.CurrentVersion, error)
```

CurrentVersion returns the latest committed value per (task, field) plus the run metadata, via DISTINCT ON. Returns (nil, nil) for an unknown run.

<a name="Store.Flush"></a>
### func (\*Store) [Flush](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/postgres/store.go#L208>)

```go
func (s *Store) Flush(runID string) error
```

Flush is a no\-op beyond confirming the transaction committed: writes are synchronous once WriteBatch returns.

<a name="Store.FullHistory"></a>
### func (\*Store) [FullHistory](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/postgres/store.go#L284>)

```go
func (s *Store) FullHistory(runID string) (*bl.FullHistory, error)
```

FullHistory returns every stored record for the run in replay order (ts, id). Returns (nil, nil) for an unknown run.

<a name="Store.WriteBatch"></a>
### func (\*Store) [WriteBatch](<https://github.com/friendly-business-machines/blkit/blob/main/stores/postgres/store.go#L150>)

```go
func (s *Store) WriteBatch(ops []bl.WriteOp) error
```

WriteBatch sends the whole batch as one pipelined round\-trip inside a single transaction via pgx.Batch — exactly the shape the worker's writer pool produces.
